recommended_option: Re-engage Belmont now to understand the fragmenting order pattern and the stopped Digital Multimeter Pro line, and work to consolidate orders back into fewer, larger baskets
headline: Belmont's orders are splitting into more, smaller baskets and one product line has gone to zero — act while it's still cheap.
rationale: Orders per month rose from 2.11 to 3.67 while lines per order fell from 3.79 to 2.18 and average order value dropped 47.3% — the classic sign of a customer starting to buy part of its basket elsewhere. DG-Digital Multimeter Pro (was Rs 11,896.85/month) has stopped entirely, and six lines together have fallen away by Rs 41,271.23/month.
why_not_more_aggressive: The account's overall revenue-at-risk is recorded as zero with priority None — a full win-back or price renegotiation is premature and would strain the relationship unnecessarily.
why_not_less_aggressive: Doing nothing wastes the cheapest moment to act — fragmentation and a stopped line can sit unnoticed before they turn into confirmed revenue loss.
expected_result: If the buyer conversation and consolidation succeed, lines per order move back toward the prior 3.79 and the Rs 41,271.23/month currently spread across six declining or stopped lines stops eroding further, even though today's system-recorded revenue-at-risk is zero.
what_to_do: Call the Belmont buyer to ask directly why DG-Digital Multimeter Pro (was Rs 11,896.85/month, now zero) stopped.
Review PT-Rotary Hammer SDS (down from Rs 20,183.50 to Rs 9,669.33/month) and PH-Precision Torque Wrench (down from Rs 9,978.66 to Rs 3,463.95/month) for signs of split sourcing.
Propose a consolidated standing order to rebuild lines-per-order from the current 2.18 back toward the prior 3.79.
Confirm Sandeep Rao as the single ongoing point of contact for Belmont following the handover from Fatima Sheikh.
Track average order value and order frequency monthly for the next quarter to catch further fragmentation early.
talking_points: Your orders per month rose from 2.11 to 3.67 while items per order fell from 3.79 to 2.18.
Digital Multimeter Pro used to be Rs 11,896.85 a month and has stopped completely.
Rotary Hammer SDS is down from Rs 20,183.50 to Rs 9,669.33 a month.
check_before_acting: Whether Digital Multimeter Pro was discontinued by Belmont themselves or is being sourced elsewhere.
Whether the account manager change from Fatima Sheikh to Sandeep Rao coincided with the fragmentation.
Whether Belmont has an alternate supplier for power tools and diagnostic equipment.
what_is_left_over: The Rs 41,271.23/month across six declining or stopped lines, including Digital Multimeter Pro at zero, remains unresolved until the buyer conversation and consolidation take effect.
downside_if_wrong: If the fragmentation reflects normal seasonal ordering rather than share loss, the outreach adds friction with no revenue benefit.
how_we_will_know_it_worked: Lines per order rise back toward 3.79 by the next quarterly review.
Average order value recovers from its current -47.3% dip by next review.
Digital Multimeter Pro (was Rs 11,896.85/month) resumes ordering or is confirmed discontinued by Belmont.
